### T-417 — Implement label and resource seed merges with ownership

> _2026-10-25 · realm/blong-core · done_

resource name.

keep hand-edited rows. Evidence: test.translation.flow steps seedLabels, reseedLabels and
editThenReseed pass; the merge predicate was renamed to seed because the generic merge shadows an
early-child realm override (F-598).

### T-692 — Decide whether core and access are carried by every process or only the ones that call them

> _2026-11-16 · realm/blong-core · done_

A `both` realm is carried by every process today, and it can now name the realms it serves instead
(k8sNeeds, @@D-871) — the mechanism is in place and blob uses it. `core` and `access` are the
largest candidates: both are `both`, so both own a process and a Service, which means a process that
does not carry one still reaches it and pays a hop rather than a copy of the triple graph, the
schema cache and the handlers. The trade is memory and startup against that hop, and the answer
needs an inventory of which realms actually call `core.*` and `access.*` in every suite the
repository deploys — a missing name is not a failure but a silent hop, which is why the list has to
be derived rather than guessed. Do it suite by suite where the measurement exists, and leave the
default alone where it does not: the realm's declaration is the same in every suite, so a list that
is right for one deployment and wrong for another is worse than no list.

Decided, and the decision is that the declaration carries the reach: the only in-process callers of
either realm outside their own packages are blong-access (super.core*, 11 sites), blong-gateway (5,
the authorize check every request runs) and blong-feedback (2, the ensure a write path calls), and
each now says so — access needs core, feedback needs core, gateway needs core and access — while
blong-login, whose methods dispatch access.* per call, names access. A realm that reaches core only
through type names (core.resource.resourceId in meta/type/schema.ts), browser page names
(access.user.profile) or a gateway authorize string dials the Service instead, which is correct and
costs a hop; party's super.core*/super.access* sites are all in adapter/dbTest, which no deployed
process runs. Nothing names core or access that should not, so both are now carried by their
declarers plus their own processes rather than by every pod, and the defaults are untouched for the
realms nobody names.
